title: Mission Contract
description: The machine-readable boundary between mission formulation and execution: this document becomes input to the existing Operator pipeline. It describes the problem/question and the bounded scope; it MUST NOT prescribe the repair unless the original source explicitly requires a specific mechanical change. Represents mission framing rejection (mission_rejected) distinctly from 'Scout found no defect'. Runtime enforcement of mission_rejected is a later slice; v0.1 defines and validates the representation.

source_candidate_id.description: Candidate this contract was opened from, when applicable.

objective.description: The decision question or objective. Must describe the problem, not prescribe the repair (e.g. 'Determine whether discrepancy X is a production defect, test defect, or another bounded cause.').

bounded_scope.description: Declared scope guidance for Scout/Repair/Review. See scope_enforcement: in v0.1 this is declared guidance, not mechanically enforced.

scope_enforcement.description: v0.1 supports only 'declared': the boundary is guidance for the roles, not mechanically enforced. A future slice may introduce mechanically enforced allowlists.

prescribes_repair.description: True only when the original source itself explicitly requires a specific mechanical change. Default false: contracts describe problems, not repairs.

policy_reference.description: Canonical policy artifact the executing roles must respect (docs/HQ_MISSION_POLICY.md).

status.description: mission_rejected is a terminal framing disposition: the mission framing/scope itself is invalid, unsafe, duplicate, unsupported, or evidence-inadequate. Distinct from Scout finding no defect.

rejection_reason.description: Reason code/reference when status is mission_rejected.

signal_ref.description: Signal reference; signal_id is the immutable HQ identity assigned at first ingestion.
